subject: Customer advisory: intermittent short-response suppression and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novapulse.com>, Novapulse Engineering <eng@novapulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Customer advisory: intermittent short-response suppression and mitigation plan

Hi Elena / Novapulse team,

Quick heads-up: since ~14:40 PT today we observed intermittent cases where short completions (responses under ~30 tokens) were being suppressed or truncated for a subset of requests routed to our hosted API. The pattern correlates with a recent KV-prefetch optimization rollout that unintentionally deprioritized small-response traffic when prefetch queue depth exceeded a threshold.

What we know so far:
- Scope: ~0.6% of requests for Novapulse in us-west-1 between 14:40–16:10 PT.
- Symptom: responses either returned an empty completion token or were cut at prompt boundary; streaming clients reported a short silence then 200 with empty text.
- Root signal: prefetch queue overflow + an LRU eviction path that suppressed prefetched prefixes for low-latency paths.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back the prefetch-deprioritization flag for us-west pools at 15:22 PT (mitigation).
- Enabled an elevated routing policy to route Novapulse traffic to a standby pool with conservative prefetch at 15:28 PT.
- Created ticket INC-2337 and opened a limited read-only postmortem draft (link below).

Attachments: small PNG of queue snapshot and an initial timeline CSV.

Next steps we will communicate: a short postmortem with root cause, corrective actions, and recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance. We are also prepared to discuss a narrow SLA credit for the impacted window if that helps.

I'll follow up with a mitigation confirmation once we validate the rollback holds. Apologies for the disruption — we know even small truncations can break production flows.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novapulse.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novapulse Engineering <eng@novapulse.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer advisory: intermittent short-response suppression and mitigation plan

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick note and mitigation steps. A couple quick asks from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether the suppression affected both streaming and non-streaming endpoints? Our mobile clients use streaming heavily.
2) We saw a spike of 502 retries from the mobile tier around 14:50 PT — is that tied to the same prefetch behavior?
3) If you recommend a client change (temporary retry/backoff), please indicate exact headers/parameters to set.

We'd like a short sync if you have capacity — 30 minutes to walk through the timeline and proposed remediation would help our on-call triage. Miguel (copied) will also pull logs from our side.

Best,
Elena

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T17:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer advisory: intermittent short-response suppression and mitigation plan

Rishi / Marissa — internal note before the sync:

- Confirmed: suppression affected both streaming and non-streaming in the affected pool; streaming timeouts manifested as short silence then an empty payload.
- Root cause summary (short): prefetched KV entries were being evicted in an LRU path when queue depth spiked; the eviction handler had a race that marked the request path as "no-prefetch" which our small-response fast-path treated as a suppressed result.
- Priority: this looks like a deployment/regression from yesterday's prefetch tuning. Engineering has a rollback ready (already executed for Novapulse) and a patch to close the race.

Action items I recommend we offer Novapulse now:
1) Short sync (30m) to walk timeline and accept logs — Rishi, can you book for tomorrow 09:00 PT?
2) Offer a 10% credit on usage for the 14:40–16:10 PT window unless legal disagrees (Marissa please confirm).
3) Provide client guidance: set Retry-After header handling with exponential backoff for 5xx and add a guard to re-request if a completion is empty within 500ms of connection close. We should draft the exact code snippet.

Marissa — can you confirm if finance needs a formal credit approval or if operations can issue a one-off concession?

Lauren

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novapulse.com>, Novapulse Engineering <eng@novapulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update and next steps — mitigation confirmed, postmortem timeline

Hi Elena / Miguel — following up with a brief update after internal review.

Status: Mitigation verified. The rollback and the routing to the conservative pool held for 24 hours without recurrence for your traffic. We've validated both streaming and non-streaming clients — logs show standard token flow and no further empty completions for the previously impacted keys.

What we will deliver to you:
- Postmortem draft (shared link): https://redwood.app/d/INC-2337-postmortem-draft — full timeline, RCA, and corrective actions (ETA: 2026-05-05 EOD).
- Client guidance snippet: short patch recommendations for handling empty completions and Retry-After semantics (included inline below).
- Financial: we are prepared to extend a one-off usage credit for the impacted window (10% of consumed tokens during 14:40–16:10 PT). Marissa, please confirm and send formal credit note by EOD.

Recommended client guidance (example):
1) If response body contains no completion tokens but HTTP 200, re-issue small backoff retry (100–300ms) up to 2 attempts.
2) For streaming clients: if delta between last token and connection close < 500ms and no completion received, attempt a reconnect with exponential jitter.

Attachments: incident-timeline-2026-05-03.csv (full request sampling) and prefetch-queue-snapshot-2026-05-01.png.

I'll schedule the 30m sync for tomorrow 09:00 PT and include engineering (Lauren invited) to walk the fix and postmortem. Please let me know if you need the credit processed sooner.

Thanks again for the patience — we'll share the postmortem and the code guidance in the next 48 hours.

Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
